quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads because they have no ground underneath. Bridges freeze first and thaw last.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Only stop if you are involved in the accident or if emergency help has not arrived. Keep driving and watch the road. Do not stop just to look at an accident.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is needed to react to things on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can hurt your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about work zones. When you see orange signs, stay alert for unsafe driving conditions. This sign tells you a flagger is ahead. You must follow their directions.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see behind your vehicle well. Be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road directly ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring straight ahead is unsafe. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often leads to risky decisions.

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky choices.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to bicycles the same way you yield to cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They expect other drivers to do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to respond.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you while driving at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: If you find yourself in a skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.question: What is the correct order of events when a school bus driver prepares to stop to load or unload children?

options.text: Amber lights flash, red lights flash, stop arm goes out, and door opens.
Red lights flash, then amber lights flash when children are loaded or unloaded.
Stop arm goes out, amber lights flash, and the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Amber lights flash, red lights flash, stop arm goes out, and door opens.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing amber lights, slow down to 20 mph or less. When red lights flash or the stop arm extends, stop at least 15 feet away. Stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing or the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights.
Use parking lights.
Use no lights.

questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is approaching. Your headlights should:

options.text: Be on high beam.
Be on low beam.
Be off. Use parking lights instead.
Be on either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is approaching or when you are following another vehicle at night. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: As you drive, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, hazmat trucks, etc.).
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, your car must be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: White lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop immediately. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These signals include flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagger, or a train horn. Do not try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down. Use your brakes lightly only after the car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that a school zone is coming up. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Always stay at your present speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When you have two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering the road. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let traffic merge.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow background and black markings. This sign warns you that wet roads are slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop for a short time to load or unload passengers.

questions.question: What do drivers need on interstate highways?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds.
To stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds safely.

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is empty.
If the right lane is full, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let the tailgater pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If tailgated, move to the right lane if empty. If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear and then slow down gradually. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: You do not need to allow as much distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry weather. Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to respond in an emergency.

questions.question: It is safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time if you are moving with other vehicles.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
questions.explanation: Always make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers.
